sections.text: During an earnings call, Elon Musk stated that Tesla is aiming to sell 5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030. This projection is actually a downgrade from his previous 2020 prediction of 20 million annual sales by 2030. Tesla has experienced back-to-back delivery declines, falling from a peak in 2023.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Achieving the 2030 goal requires a 25 percent compound annual growth rate. However, Tesla relies heavily on just two vehicles, discontinued older models, faced declining sales, and abandoned plans for a cheaper mass-market electric vehicle. Furthermore, reaching 5 million cars demands doubling current factory space, and the alternative strategy relies heavily on unapproved autonomous robotaxis.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.text: Indian actor and director Nana Patekar died aged 75 of a heart attack. Known for his intense performances and versatility across heroic and villainous roles, he rose to international prominence in Mira Nair’s Salaam Bombay! and starred in major Bollywood hits including Parinda and Krantiveer. His later career involved philanthropic work through the Naam Foundation, alongside a return to screen acting after facing sexual harassment allegations raised by Tanushree Dutta.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Patekar was regarded as a towering figure in Indian cinema, remaining alongside Irrfan Khan as the only performer to win Filmfare’s best actor, best supporting actor and best villain awards. His rougher edges and naturalistic style brought street realism to Bollywood. However, accusations made by his former co-star Tanushree Dutta in 2018 kickstarted India’s #MeToo movement, permanently altering the conversation around his legacy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Premature twins Raghad and Raad fled with their family on foot for three days as fighting surged in Yemen. Arriving at al-Sadaqah hospital in Aden, they were diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition driven by conflict and poverty.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The collapse of an informal ceasefire has intensified the conflict, displacing thousands and cutting off aid to hundreds of thousands of people, leaving vulnerable children caught in the middle of a hunger crisis.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hospital staff continue treating critical cases under severe constraints, while displaced families face ongoing poverty, lack of resources, and the risk of recurring illness for their children.
